title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: the opening page of Chapter II, 'Réalisations topologiques des réseaux', dated 6 June 1986. It lays the point-set groundwork for realizing combinatorial 'réseaux' by topological cells. (1) For a topological space X and a closed subset A, X/A is the quotient collapsing A to a point a. If X' ⊂ X contains A, then the natural map X'/A → X/A is a topological embedding. Grothendieck's justification: closed sets of X'/A are the closed Y' ⊂ X' that are saturated, i.e. Y'∩A ∈ {∅, A}. These are exactly the traces on X' of saturated closed sets Y of X, which are the closed sets of X/A. (2) Definition: A is 'régulièrement immergé' (regularly embedded) in X if the point a has a closed conical neighbourhood in X/A. That is, there is a closed neighbourhood V of a and a homeomorphism h: V ≅ Cone(B), with B a compact space, h(a) equal to the cone vertex o, and h^{-1}(cone minus base), i.e. V minus B, open in X/A. (3) The cone structure gives the shrunken cones tV = V_t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1. For t in ]0,1] these are homeomorphic to V. The next page makes the further claims: the V_t form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of a; their preimages W_t form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of A in X; B_t is the frontier of W_t; and X minus B_t is the topological sum of the interior of W_t and the exterior X minus V_t. Further remarks there: the notion is local in X; it makes sense for A = ∅ (with X/∅ = {a} ⊔ X and B = ∅); it holds for (triangulable) subspaces of manifolds. The page then defines a 'cellule topologique' as a space X with an unordered pair {A, B} of subsets. In modern terms, 'A regularly immersed' says A has a mapping-cylinder/collar-type neighbourhood: a neighbourhood W with W minus A ≅ B × ]0,1], with ends controlled by the compact 'link' B. This is the point-set preparation for building cell structures, i.e. topological realizations of combinatorial networks, in the spirit of tame topology.
errors: No real error. The embedding claim X'/A → X/A is correct for any subset X' ⊇ A, and the argument given is correct.

The fundamental-system claims are correct only because B is assumed compact; the tube lemma is needed for the shrunken cones to be cofinal among neighbourhoods of the vertex. The page uses this compactness implicitly. Correspondingly, every open set containing A is saturated, so neighbourhoods of A in X correspond exactly to neighbourhoods of a.
Minor point: the condition 'h(V minus B) open' really asks that B, the image of the cone's base, be the frontier of V in X/A. This is stated only implicitly.

ideas.what: Quotient X/A restricted to a subspace X' ⊇ A is a subspace of X/A; closed sets of X/A are the saturated closed sets
A closed subset is 'regularly immersed' if the collapsed point has a closed conical neighbourhood Cone(B) with compact link B
ideas.modern_name: conical / mapping-cylinder neighbourhood; collared or regular neighbourhood; locally cone-like (Siebenmann) structure; local conic structure in o-minimal geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.H.C. Whitehead (regular neighbourhoods); Siebenmann (1972); Quinn (mapping cylinder neighbourhoods); van den Dries and others (o-minimal conic structure)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the 'topologie modérée' section of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this definition

ideas.what: Convention X/∅ = {a} ⊔ X, so that the notion makes sense for A empty (with B = ∅)
A topological cell defined as a space X with an unordered pair {A, B} of subsets, with A, B presumably regularly immersed, as a building block for realizing 'réseaux'
ideas.modern_name: cell with two ends / bicone- or join-type cell; stratified cell decompositions

missed.claim: Beginning of a programme to give topological realizations of combinatorial 'réseaux' using cells (X,{A,B}) whose distinguished subsets have conical (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhoods. This is a concrete attempt at the tame-topology foundations announced in the Esquisse, carried out in a 1986 manuscript chapter that seems unstudied.
missed.quote: On dit que A est régulièrement immergé dans X si ∃ voisinage conique fermé de a dans X/A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could be compared with o-minimal / stratified-space approaches (Siebenmann, Quinn, Lurie's conically smooth stratified spaces) to see whether Grothendieck's cell formalism anticipates or differs from them. On this page itself the content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only standard point-set topology: quotient by a closed set, and conical or mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods. Its interest is mainly as the start of an unpublished 1986 chapter on topological realizations of 'réseaux' related to tame topology.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Réalisations topologiques des réseaux' (as in the archive cote), not 'vitraux'.
Section heading '1. Ficelle topologique' is very likely '1. Cellule topologique', consistent with the definition on the next page.
'par considérations les' should read 'par considérant les' or similar.
'(contrôle[?] des cônes)' is uncertain; possibly '(cônes des cônes)' or '(centre des cônes)'.
The left-margin notes are largely illegible; they contain 'NB V̇ = B' and 'NB V̇_t = B_t' (the boundary of V is B).
